_INSTRUCTIONS_FOR_ANY_AI_OR_DEVELOPER_ED: Every time you change this app, add ONE entry to the top of the 'entries'
array below. It renders as the Update Log on the League Admin page, and it
is how the two people running this pool keep track of what changed and when.
Do not skip it for small changes. A one-line CSS fix still gets an entry.
Use the COMMIT time of the change. `git log --date=iso-strict`
gives it. Never invent or estimate a time -- these are read as
"title":  Short plain-English summary. What changed, not how.
"detail": One or two sentences. Say why, and name anything a league
member would actually notice. Optional but strongly preferred.
a record of when things actually shipped.
"by":     Who made the change: "Dave", "Caleb", or the AI's name.
Keep entries factual. This log is read by people deciding whether something
broke, so do not describe work that was not actually finished and shipped.

entries.title: The home team is marked with an @
entries.detail: The picks page now puts an @ on the home team’s row, so a game reads "KC @ BUF" straight down. Worth having because the spread’s sign is quoted against the home team — –2.5 on the @ row means that team is laying 2.5 — and which team that was had to be inferred from row order alone.

entries.title: Picked teams wear their own colours again
entries.detail: The team you pick now fills its row with diagonal stripes in that team’s primary and secondary colours, the way the old board did, instead of a flat wash of the primary. A dark scrim sits over the stripes so the name and the spread stay readable even behind Steelers gold or Chargers yellow.

entries.title: Rebuilt the picks page around the spread
entries.detail: Each game is now two stacked team rows with the spread in its own right-hand column, three times the size it was, so the two numbers line up and the favourite reads at a glance. Kickoff time and the over/under moved to one dim line underneath. A game is 112px on desktop and 139px on a phone, down from 175px and 275px before the rework started.

entries.title: Pick rows are half the height, and sort by points
entries.detail: Each game's spread now sits on the team button instead of a separate bar, and the total, kickoff and score share one line. Nine games fit on a desktop screen instead of five, four on a phone instead of two. A new control beside the week heading sorts by kickoff or by the points you've assigned, highest or lowest first.

entries.title: Fixed tabs getting stuck on “Loading…”
entries.detail: On a weak connection a page could hang on “Loading…” forever — and stay stuck even once the signal came back, so the only fix was switching tabs and returning. Requests now give up after 12 seconds and show a Try again button, and a stalled page reloads itself when you come back online or reopen the app.

entries.title: Games whose spread moved are highlighted
entries.detail: If the line changes after you pick, the whole game box turns yellow and shows both numbers — the spread you took and the current one — with a button to switch to the current one if you want it. Your pick is judged against the line you took unless you press it.

entries.title: Spreads refresh again, and your pick remembers the line you took
entries.detail: Spreads had stopped updating entirely once every game had a number — hence “2 days ago”. They now re-check about once an hour while anyone has the app open. Each pick also records the spread and over/under showing when you made it, and whether you covered is judged against that number rather than wherever the line drifted to afterwards.

entries.title: Points already in use are marked, and reordering asks first
entries.detail: The points dropdown now shows which numbers are taken — “13 (used)” — as a reference, while still letting you pick them. Choosing one asks before it moves the other games, naming which game currently holds that number and how many will shift.

entries.title: Changing a game's points now reorders the rest
entries.detail: You no longer have to clear another game first. Pick any number and the games in between shift a step to make room — move a game from 13 up to 16 and the ones that held 16, 15 and 14 slide down to 15, 14 and 13. Games that have already kicked off keep their points, so any move that would disturb one isn't offered.

entries.title: The picks page shows how fresh the spreads are
entries.detail: A line under the week heading says where the spreads and over/unders came from and when — “pulled from ESPN 40m ago” or “published by an admin 2h ago” — with a Refresh button to check again on the spot.

entries.title: Fixed the times on this Update Log
entries.detail: The older entries were backfilled with estimated times rather than real ones — some were two days out. Every entry now carries the actual time the change shipped, shown in Eastern, and updates that shipped together are grouped under one timestamp instead of repeating the same clock.

entries.title: Fixed the app bogging down while making picks
entries.detail: Every single tap was re-uploading the whole season (about 80 KB) and re-reading the league roster twice. Filling in one week meant 64 database operations and 1.3 MB uploaded. Saves are now batched shortly after you stop clicking, and the roster scan only runs when it can actually matter — the same week of picks is now 3 operations and one upload. Anything still unsaved is written immediately if you close or background the app.

entries.title: The pool now runs on Eastern time
entries.detail: Kickoffs and lock times are shown in ET no matter where your phone thinks it is. Two real bugs went with it: the weekly 6:00 AM unlock was 6am on each person's own clock, so the week opened at different moments for people in different timezones, and the board flipped to the next week at about 8pm ET on Monday — during Monday Night Football — because it was using UTC dates.

entries.title: Survivor is now double elimination
entries.detail: Your first losing lock is a strike and you stay in; the second ends your Survivor season. The board shows an amber “1 strike — 1 left” state between alive and out, and the standings and admin roster show each person's strike count.

entries.title: Survivor view on the Group Picks grid
entries.detail: A Confidence / Survivor toggle. Survivor shows the whole season: weeks down the left, everyone across the top, each cell the team they locked with a green ring if it won and red if it lost, plus a running strike count under each name. Other people's locks stay hidden until that team kicks off.

entries.title: Added a Group Picks grid
entries.detail: New Group Picks tab: games down the left, everyone across the top, each cell showing the logo of the team they took with their wager printed over it. Correct picks get a green ring once the game is graded, wrong ones red. Other people's picks stay hidden until each game kicks off — they aren't just hidden on screen, they aren't published until then. Your own column is always visible.

entries.title: Fixed renaming your team creating a second roster entry
entries.detail: Roster rows were filed under your team name, so changing it wrote a brand new row and left the old one behind — you appeared twice in the standings. Rows are now filed under your account id, which never changes, and any duplicate left by the old behaviour is cleaned up automatically on your next sync.

entries.title: Added this Update Log
entries.detail: A running, timestamped list of what has changed, shown on the League Admin page so both admins can see what shipped and when.

entries.title: Added a Research tab and a finish-your-profile gate
entries.detail: New Research tab, plus a prompt to complete your profile before picking.

entries.title: Moved the spread and results editors onto the Admin page
entries.detail: Both editors now live on League Admin with a week selector, instead of being buried in the week view.

entries.title: Spread update
entries.detail: Spread and schedule corrections.

entries.title: Results editor pulls final scores from ESPN
entries.detail: A Fetch results from ESPN button fills in each finished game's winner, shows the final score, and works out the Monday Night combined total. You still review and press Save & Publish.

entries.title: Fixed the page only scrolling from the scrollbar
entries.detail: An overflow rule turned the page into a container that sized to its own content, so there was nothing for a wheel or touch drag to scroll.

entries.title: Spreads and over/unders now appear without an admin publishing them
entries.detail: Any game missing a line fills itself in from ESPN. An admin-published number still overrides it.

entries.title: Live scores and automatic grading
entries.detail: Each game shows its score and who won by how much, and finished games grade themselves. An admin correction still wins.

entries.title: Signed-in sessions now stick to your device
entries.detail: You stay logged in until you press Log Out, instead of being signed out every time the app closed.

entries.title: Installable on a phone, and usable on one
entries.detail: Add to Home Screen support with offline loading, plus a mobile layout — the page used to scroll sideways and most buttons were too small to tap.

entries.title: Games lock at their own kickoff instead of all at once
entries.detail: Missing Thursday night no longer costs you the rest of the week, and submitting a lineup no longer freezes it. Survivor stays open all week but only lets you pick teams that have not played yet.

entries.title: Rebuilt the app from one file into modules
entries.detail: The whole board was a single 4,226-line HTML file. Schedule, teams, week dates and rules moved into data files, the code split into modules, and a 249 KB image came out of the stylesheet.
